recognize_zh: 血液抹片中數顆紅血球被寄生蟲幾乎填滿，蟲體呈圓形、紫藍色、細胞質內散布細小棕色瘧色素，被感染的紅血球與周圍正常紅血球同大或略大，下方四張放大圖以配子體與成熟滋養體為主；配合旅遊史，符合間日瘧（Plasmodium vivax）感染。
features: Several parasitized RBCs containing large rounded parasites that fill most of the red cell
Parasite cytoplasm blue-purple with dispersed fine golden-brown hemozoin pigment and pinkish-red chromatin
Infected RBCs normal-sized to slightly enlarged compared with neighboring uninfected cells
Magnified insets 1-4 show round gametocytes and mature amoeboid trophozoites
No multiple small ring forms or banana-shaped gametocytes; a normal band/segmented neutrophil at right
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood film shows scattered parasitized red cells among otherwise unremarkable erythrocytes and a neutrophil. The infected red cells are normal to slightly enlarged and contain large round to amoeboid parasites with blue cytoplasm, pink chromatin and fine dispersed brown pigment, representing mature trophozoites and round gametocytes as highlighted in the enlarged insets. Multiply infected cells, appliqué rings and crescent-shaped gametocytes are not seen. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection; Schüffner stippling is not clearly resolved at this magnification, and species confirmation by PCR or a reference laboratory is recommended, as was performed here.

ddx.vs: P. ovale also enlarges RBCs and shows Schüffner dots but infected cells are oval with fimbriated edges and the parasite is more compact.
P. malariae infects normal-sized or small RBCs with coarse dark pigment and characteristic band-form trophozoites and rosette schizonts.
P. falciparum shows numerous small delicate rings, multiply infected RBCs and banana-shaped gametocytes, with mature stages rarely seen in peripheral blood.
Babesia forms small pleomorphic rings or Maltese cross tetrads without hemozoin pigment or gametocytes.
